skill.name: azure-mgmt-apimanagement-dotnet
skill.description: Guides .NET developers through Azure Resource Manager API Management tasks, including services, APIs, products, subscriptions, policies, backups, and SDK references.
skill.summary: Build and manage Azure API Management resources with the .NET Azure Resource Manager SDK.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, and Azure credential variable names, but these are documentation examples rather than executed code. One semantic issue remains: the subscription example prints an APIM primary key to console output. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: The subscription example prints an APIM primary key to console output.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the key print statement, mask the value, or direct users to store subscription keys in Azure Key Vault.

remediation.issue: Setup examples mention service principal secret variables.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning to avoid committing secrets and to prefer managed identity or secure local secret storage.

remediation.issue: Installation commands are presented inside the skill documentation.
remediation.suggestion: State that package installation commands are examples for user-approved project setup, not automatic agent actions.

semantic_findings.title: Secret Exposure in Example Output
semantic_findings.description: The subscription example retrieves APIM subscription secrets and prints the primary key to console output. Users may copy this pattern into scripts that leak keys into logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly calls GetSecretsAsync and writes keys.Value.PrimaryKey to Console.WriteLine. APIM subscription keys are credentials, so console output can expose secrets.

content.value_statement: Azure API Management projects require many resource-specific SDK calls. This skill gives focused .NET ARM SDK patterns for services, APIs, products, subscriptions, policies, and backups.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Azure.ResourceManager.ApiManagement for management-plane APIM work.
Shows package installation and DefaultAzureCredential setup for .NET projects.
Outlines the APIM resource hierarchy from subscriptions to services, APIs, products, and gateways.
Provides C# patterns for creating services, APIs, products, subscriptions, policies, backups, and restores.
Links to official Microsoft documentation for APIM, policy reference, and SDK reference.
limitations: Does not cover data-plane calls to APIM gateway endpoints.
Does not execute Azure commands or validate live cloud resources.
Uses sample names, locations, and URLs that must be replaced before production use.
Does not include every API Management feature or policy option.

use_cases.title: Provision APIM Services
use_cases.description: Create and configure API Management service instances with the .NET Azure Resource Manager SDK.

use_cases.title: Publish Managed APIs
use_cases.description: Add backend APIs, define products, and connect subscriptions inside an existing APIM service.

use_cases.title: Plan Governance Workflows
use_cases.description: Map policies, products, users, groups, gateways, backups, and restore steps for managed API platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Service
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new APIM instance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create a Developer SKU Azure API Management service in .NET. Include authentication setup and required Azure resource names.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Backend API
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add an HTTPS backend API to an existing APIM service using the .NET ARM SDK. Explain the resource hierarchy and required identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Products and Policies
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced access control and throttling workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET workflow that creates a product, adds an API to it, creates a subscription, and applies rate limiting. Include long-running operations and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review APIM Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned APIM management-plane automation for services, APIs, products, policies, backup, and restore. Identify SDK classes, ordering constraints, and production risks.

output_examples.input: I need a new APIM service for a development environment.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step .NET ARM SDK plan covering authentication, resource group lookup, service settings, SKU choice, and long-running operation handling.

output_examples.input: I want to publish a backend API and expose it through a product.
output_examples.output: A guided workflow that creates the API, creates a product, associates the API with the product, and describes subscription requirements.

output_examples.input: I need to add rate limiting and prepare backup steps.
output_examples.output: A production checklist that covers policy placement, XML format choice, backup parameters, managed identity access, and restore validation.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and managed identities where possible.
Replace sample identifiers and URLs with environment-specific values before deployment.
Avoid printing subscription keys; handle secrets through secure storage and short-lived access.
anti_patterns: Using this management-plane SDK for runtime gateway calls.
Copying sample publisher emails, resource names, or URLs into production.
Writing APIM subscription keys or client secrets to terminal output or logs.

faq.question: What Azure SDK package does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.ResourceManager.ApiManagement for .NET management-plane operations.

faq.question: Does this skill call live Azure services by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples; users or agents must run any project code separately.

faq.question: Can it help create an API Management service?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes the main SDK objects and workflow for creating an APIM service resource.

faq.question: Does it cover APIM gateway data-plane requests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Azure Resource Manager operations, not runtime gateway calls.

faq.question: Which authentication approach is recommended?
faq.answer: The skill recommends DefaultAzureCredential and warns against hardcoded keys.

faq.question: Can it help with policies and subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for policy creation, product setup, and subscription management.
